basics.local_name: Bosna i Hercegovina / Босна и Херцеговина
basics.regime_2024: Currency board: KM 1.95583 per euro, fully reserve-backed
basics.central_bank: Central Bank of Bosnia and Herzegovina (CBBH)

policy_rate.note: Currency board — the CBBH sets no policy rate; it imports the ECB's stance.

events.text: The High Representative imposes changes to the election law and the Federation constitution as polls close.
The UN General Assembly adopts the Srebrenica genocide resolution; 11 July becomes a day of remembrance.
The worst floods and landslides in years cut off Jablanica; a quarry collapses on Donja Jablanica.
Republika Srpska president Milorad Dodik is sentenced to a year in prison and a six-year ban from office for defying the High Representative.
The US Treasury lifts sanctions on Dodik, his family and allies.
Dodik ally Siniša Karan wins the snap Republika Srpska presidential election with 50.39%.

since_2024.text: Growth stayed near 2%: the central bank's nowcast put Q3 2025 at 1.9% and Q4 2025 at 2.1% year on year.
Inflation picked up again — 4.2% in Q4 2025 and 4.9% year on year in August 2026.
The 4 October 2026 general election (preliminary) returned Bećirović, Filipović and Cvijanović to the Presidency on 41.5% turnout.
Ratings held steady: S&P B+ stable (affirmed 31 July 2026), Moody's B3 stable.

did_you_know.text: The KM 10–100 notes come in two designs, one for the Federation and one for Republika Srpska — both are valid everywhere.
The coastline is only about 20 km long, at Neum.
Chinese tourist arrivals rose from 5,234 in 2022 to 74,996 in 2024.
In 2024 Turkey sent 205,831 tourists — almost four times Germany's 56,094.

policy_rate.note: Monetary policy rate; cut from 2.0% to 1.75% for Q2 2024.

events.text: The IMF approves a three-year Extended Fund Facility (about $56m) and a Resilience and Sustainability Facility (about $46m).
A per-night tourism environmental sustainability levy (SCR 25–100) takes effect.
The EU adds Seychelles to its list of non-cooperative tax jurisdictions.
The EU moves Seychelles off the blacklist and onto its grey list.
The central bank makes its first cut of the period, from 2.0% to 1.75%.
Patrick Herminie (United Seychelles) defeats President Wavel Ramkalawan in the run-off, 52.7% to 47.3%.

since_2024.text: A record 398,841 visitors arrived in 2025, up 13%.
The IMF completed its fifth and sixth programme reviews on 26 May 2026; it puts growth at 5.1% in 2025 and 1.5% in 2026.
About 60% of visitors transit Doha, Dubai or Abu Dhabi, which leaves arrivals exposed to Middle East air disruption.
Fitch upgraded Seychelles to BB in September 2025, its highest rating since 2019.

did_you_know.text: Seychelles issued the world's first sovereign blue bond — $15m, in October 2018.
The coco de mer of the Vallée de Mai has the largest seed in the plant kingdom.
It is the least populous sovereign country in Africa.
It spent October 2023 to February 2024 on the EU's tax blacklist.

basics.local_name: Việt Nam (Cộng hòa Xã hội chủ nghĩa Việt Nam)
basics.regime_2024: Managed: the State Bank sets a daily central rate with a ±5% band (widened October 2022)

policy_rate.note: Refinancing rate: 6% from 25 October 2022, 4.5% from 19 June 2023.

events.text: President Nguyễn Xuân Phúc resigns, the most senior casualty of the “blazing furnace” anti-corruption drive.
Tô Lâm becomes Party General Secretary after Nguyễn Phú Trọng's death on 19 July.
The US announces a 46% “reciprocal” tariff on Viet Nam; a 2 July deal sets it at 20% (40% on transshipment).
Provinces are merged from 63 to 34 and the district tier is abolished.
FTSE Russell announces an upgrade from Frontier to Secondary Emerging market, effective 21 September 2026.
The 14th Party Congress closes and re-elects Tô Lâm General Secretary for 2026–31.

since_2024.text: GDP grew 8.02% in 2025 with CPI inflation at 3.31% (GSO).
First-half 2026 GDP rose 8.18%; average CPI was 4.38%, and June's year-on-year rate 4.69%.
The World Bank moved Viet Nam to upper-middle income on 1 July 2026.
Moody's turned its outlook positive in May 2026; S&P and Fitch still rate Viet Nam one notch below investment grade.

did_you_know.text: Viet Nam is the world's second-largest coffee producer, and robusta is about 95% of its output.
Sơn Đoòng, the world's largest cave, was only surveyed in 2009.
Electronics exports topped $100bn in 2025; the US alone bought about $153bn of goods.

basics.regime_2024: De facto US-dollar peg near MVR 15.4 (official ±20% band around 12.85)

policy_rate.note: The MMA publishes no single policy rate; its standing deposit (1.5%) and lending (10%) facility rates were unchanged through 2022–24.

events.text: President Muizzu's PNC wins a parliamentary supermajority.
Tax rises are ratified: the green tax doubles to $12 a night from January 2025 and tourism GST rises to 17% from July 2025.
The China–Maldives free trade agreement, signed in 2014, enters into force.
On Narendra Modi's visit India extends a ₹4,850 crore line of credit, and the two sides agree terms for an FTA.
Airspace closures during the Middle East war cut March arrivals by 20.7% year on year.
A $500m sukuk is repaid from the Sovereign Development Fund and reserves.

since_2024.text: Inflation reached 4.04% in 2025, a 13-year high, driven by food and tobacco duties.
Foreign-exchange reserves recovered to $859m in October 2025 from a $364m low in September 2024.
Arrivals hit a record 2.25 million in 2025, then fell 4.3% year on year over January–August 2026.
Fitch upgraded the Maldives to CCC- after the sukuk repayment, while flagging its exposure to the energy shock.

did_you_know.text: From 1 November 2025 no one born on or after 1 January 2007 may buy tobacco — the first nationwide generational ban.
In October 2009 the cabinet met underwater to draw attention to climate change.
It repaid a $500m sukuk in April 2026 while Fitch still rated it CC.
